How a change at Newspoll cast a shadow over the PM

In mid 2015 the Newspoll organisation, which had been doing national polls since 1985, was closed down by its owners. A separate research company, Galaxy, was commissioned to run the poll using the Newspoll name and questions but with big changes to how the data was collected.

Galaxy increased the sample size from an average of around 1,150 interviews a poll to around 1,700 (although it varies). While the old Newspoll was conducted by live interviewers, the new Newspoll uses automated pre-recorded questions (where people push buttons on their phone to provide responses) supplemented by an online panel.

The old Newspoll moved around a bit. From the time Abbott became Opposition Leader in December 2009 to June 2015 the Newspoll two-party preferred vote moved an average of 1.9 per cent from poll to poll. Less than one in five (16 per cent) of the old Newspolls showed zero change from the previous poll. The new Galaxy-Newspoll moves a lot less. Its average movement from poll to poll is 0.8 per cent and more than two in five polls (44 per cent) show zero movement at all on the two-party preferred vote. Compared with the old Newspoll that's less than half the average movement and almost three times the frequency of polls with no change at all. So the Galaxy-Newspoll is a much less variable poll.
